supported_by_reopened_source: A direct .run() call on a base threading.Thread synchronously calls the stored self._target with stored self._args/self._kwargs in the calling frame, gated only by 'self._target is not None'.
Thread.__init__ stores target, args and kwargs by reference (925-928); kwargs None becomes {} (912-913); args default is () (881).
Thread.start()'s worker path calls self._context.run(self.run) (1082), so start and direct run share the run body.
Timer.run() blocks in self.finished.wait(self.interval), calls self.function(*self.args, **self.kwargs) only if 'not self.finished.is_set()', then always sets finished (1382-1386).
Timer.cancel() is exactly self.finished.set() (1378-1380), so a sequential cancel before run suppresses the function call for that run.
